paper.title_en: Recurrent Fourier Neural Operator for Event-by-Event Relativistic Hydrodynamics
paper.abstract_en: Relativistic hydrodynamics is a powerful tool to simulate the evolution of the quark--gluon plasma (QGP) in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, but event-by-event simulations are computationally demanding, especially for Bayesian analyses. We develop a recurrent Fourier neural operator (rFNO) that emulates the evolution of $(2+1)$-dimensional relativistic hydrodynamics. Three networks are trained on the $32\times32$, $64\times64$, and $128\times128$ lattices using profiles of the same \textsc{VISH2+1} hydrodynamic events up to $τ-τ_0=4.8~\mathrm{fm}/c$. The networks trained on the coarser lattices are then directly evaluated on the $128\times128$ lattice without retraining, while the $128\times128$ network provides the native-resolution reference. A comparison with the \textsc{VISH2+1} results shows that the rFNO predictions across resolutions nicely capture the magnitude and structures of the temperature profiles, and describe the event-by-event eccentricities $\varepsilon_n$ ($n=2,3,4$), the momentum anisotropy $\varepsilon_p$, and their time evolution within the supervised proper-time interval. After the recurrent continuation to $τ-τ_0=6.4~\mathrm{fm}/c$, the relative errors of the predicted $\varepsilon_n$ and $\varepsilon_p$ remain within about $10\%$. These results demonstrate that the rFNO realizes zero-shot super-resolution predictions for relativistic hydrodynamics and can be recurrently continued beyond the supervised interval.
